A 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis of 1 month's duration. The swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an 'orange' over 4 days. Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement.

Because of persistent hematuria and suspected stent occlusion, cystoscopy and ureteral stent exchange were performed: removal of the right double-J catheter revealed pulsatile arterial bleeding from the right ureteral orifice. The stent was changed, bleeding subsided, and she received four units of packed red cells intraoperatively. Open surgery was considered too high risk.

A CT angiogram demonstrated active hemorrhage at the right renal pelvis with clots in the collecting system. The patient was hemodynamically stable and managed expectantly, but that night she had recurrent gross hematuria. Embolisation of the right renal artery with coils was performed. During subsequent left stent repositioning, retrograde ureterography revealed a ureteroileal fistula, and a new ureteral catheter was placed; conservative management was advised. Within 24 hours, massive hematuria recurred and her hemoglobin continued to fall despite further transfusion.

vignette:
A 36-year-old woman with a 17-year history of migraine headaches was referred for management of a right-sided migraine characterized by a visual aura of gray-white spots followed by pain behind the right eye radiating to the right frontal, temporal, and suboccipital regions. She typically had 3 to 4 severe migraines per month lasting 3 to 7 days, with relief only from sumatriptan after trials of acetaminophen, ibuprofen, rizatriptan, methylprednisolone, prednisone, and dexamethasone failed. In January 2023, she developed a right orbital and medial cheek headache radiating to the right lateral jaw, ear, and down the right suboccipital region. Treatment with ketorolac, rizatriptan, and a 7-day dexamethasone taper failed to resolve her symptoms. She then received naratriptan, prochlorperazine, acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and diphenhydramine without improvement. Brain magnetic resonance imaging was unremarkable. Given refractory symptoms, she underwent an ultrasound-guided right sphenopalatine ganglion block with 4 mL of bupivacaine 0.25% and 1 mL of dexamethasone 4 mg/mL. This treatment also failed to resolve her symptoms.
